scaling.note: the lattice per-query cost is flat in the table size; the scan grows with N, so the ratio grows with N

notes: At point-query volume the lattice wins 3.5x at 100M rows, up from 1.54x at 9.9M rows.
The lattice per-query cost is independent of the table size (0.311 ms at 9.9M, 0.312 ms at 100M), the ExaVerif pattern: the subspace, not the space.
The matrix P3 point is capped at 1 ms by the CLI timer resolution; the volume measurement is the reliable comparison.
Wide queries still lose through the table function vehicle (S1 46,225 rows at 155 ms against 3 ms for the scan); the lattice is a point-lookup access path.
The gain scales with N; a 1B-row table would raise the ratio further.
